title: Cloud Resource Tagging Compliance

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:config:notification` events with `resourceType="AWS::EC2::Instance"` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.4.4 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:config:notification` traffic without `resourceType="AWS::EC2::Instance"`. Confirm UC-4.4.4 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:config:notification` collected via Cloud provider TAs, Config rules; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" resourceType="AWS::EC2::Instance"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.4_cloud_resource_tagging_c_4"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.4.4 — Cloud Resource Tagging Compliance: queries Microsoft Azure `aws:config:notification` for search criteria `resourceType="AWS::EC2::Instance"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, missing governance tags for 'Cloud Resource Tagging Compliance' break cost allocation, environment scoping, and incident routing—delaying containment when resources cannot be classified quickly. UC-4.4.4 drives low-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Use AWS Config rules (required-tags), Azure Policy, or GCP org policies to evaluate tagging. Ingest compliance results. Dashboard showing tagging compliance by tag and resource type.
visualization: Table (resource, missing tags), Pie chart (compliant %), Bar chart by tag.
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure Cloud provider TAs, Config rules with the modular input for `aws:config:notification`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Use AWS Config rules (required-tags), Azure Policy, or GCP org policies to evaluate tagging. Ingest compliance results. Dashboard showing tagging compliance by tag and resource type.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" resourceType="AWS::EC2::Instance"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.4_cloud_resource_tagging_c_4"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:config:notification` in `index=aws` to detect cloud resource tagging compliance. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_4_alert` with severity aligned to `low` criticality. Dashboard: Table (resource, missing tags), Pie chart (compliant %), Bar chart by tag..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Cloud provider TAs, Config rules and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloud resource tagging compliance so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
